question.problem:
The values of functions $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=2$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $q(x)$ | $r(x)$ | ${q}^{′}(x)$ | ${r}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $4$ | $-1$ | $-3$ | $2$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))$ at $x=2.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))|}_{x=2}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))=3{q}^{′}(x)+4{r}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))|}_{x=2} & =3{q}^{′}(2)+4{r}^{′}(2) \\  & =3(-3)+4(2) \\  & =-9+8 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
